author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Jaden Hill (shoulder) yet to begin throwing
desc: Jaden Hill has been completing rehab exercises but has yet to resume throwing.
impact: Hill landed on the injured list June 24 due to right shoulder tendinitis. He is still in the early stages of recovery and has not yet resumed throwing. A clear timeline remains unavailable, and fantasy managers should not expect one until he begins a throwing progression.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Clay Holmes (fibula) to throw off mound this week
desc: Clay Holmes has been throwing on flat ground and hopes to throw off the mound sometime this week.
impact: Holmes fractured his right fibula on a comebacker May 15. He began throwing just over two weeks ago and has made steady progress in his recovery. However, fantasy managers should not expect him to return until August.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Blake Dunn (elbow) receives cortisone injection
desc: Blake Dunn received a cortisone injection.
impact: Dunn landed on the 10-day injured list June 28 with a right elbow sprain. He is expected to rest briefly before beginning a hitting and throwing progression. He remains without a clear timeline for return.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Patrick Sandoval (biceps) to make next rehab start Saturday
desc: Patrick Sandoval is scheduled to make his next minor league rehab start on Saturday.
impact: Sandoval last pitched on Sunday with Triple-A Worcester, allowing one run on three hits over four innings. His scheduled rehab start on Saturday could be his final outing before joining the Boston Red Sox rotation.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Nick Pivetta (elbow) throws light bullpen session Saturday
desc: Nick Pivetta threw a light bullpen session on Saturday.
impact: Pivetta has been sidelined since April 14 with a flexor strain. He began playing catch in late May and has since completed his first bullpen session. He will need multiple bullpen sessions and will likely face live hitters before beginning a minor league rehab assignment. Fantasy managers should not expect him to return before the All-Star break.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Willy Adames (back) MRI reveals no structural damage
desc: Willy Adames underwent an MRI on Monday that revealed no structural damage.
impact: Adames exited Sunday's 3-2 win over the Atlanta Braves with lower back spasms. He was unable to return to the lineup Monday against the Arizona Diamondbacks, but the good news is that MRI results revealed no structural damage. He avoided a significant injury, and it remains unclear if he'll require a stint on the injured list. For now, fantasy managers can consider him day-to-day, with his next chance to return coming on Tuesday.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Keaton Winn (elbow) throws bullpen session Monday
desc: Keaton Winn threw a 25-pitch bullpen session on Monday.
impact: Winn was placed on the injured list June 14 with a right elbow strain. He followed up a 20-pitch bullpen session on Friday with a 25-pitch session on Monday. He is scheduled to begin rehab games in the Arizona Complex League later this week.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Joel Peguero (hamstring) throws bullpen session Monday
desc: Joel Peguero threw a 30-pitch bullpen session on Monday.
impact: Peguero was placed on the 60-day injured list June 1 with a left hamstring strain. He threw bullpen sessions on Friday and Monday as he continues to progress in his recovery. It's unclear whether he'll face live hitters next or throw another bullpen session.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Jakob Junis (heat exhaustion) to avoid IL
desc: Jakob Junis was pulled from Monday's contest against the Cleveland Guardians due to heat exhaustion.
impact: Junis exited while warming up before the eighth inning following a visit from Texas Rangers manager Skip Schumaker. He had thrown 16 pitches in the seventh inning. Fantasy managers should consider him day-to-day.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Stefan Raeth released by Mariners
impact: Raeth had been pitching in Double-A Arkansas. He could seek another opportunity.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Cooper Criswell (shoulder) to undergo MRI July 6
desc: Mariners GM Justin Hollander said Cooper Criswell will undergo an MRI on July 6.
impact: The Mariners should have an update on Criswell by the middle of July. Hollander said he is still anticipating a return for him in mid-to-late August.

author: Ari Koslow
title: Matt Brash (lat) to undergo MRI July 6
desc: Mariners GM Justin Hollander said Matt Brash will undergo an MRI on July 6.
impact: The Mariners should have an update on Brash by the middle of July. Hollander said he is still anticipating a return for him in mid-to-late August.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Xavier Edwards records stolen base Monday
desc: Xavier Edwards went 1-for-5 with a run scored and a stolen base in Monday's 10-7 win over the Colorado Rockies.
impact: Edwards had a relatively quiet game Monday considering the Miami Marlins scored 10 runs, but he still provided fantasy managers with some production. He singled to right field in the fifth inning, stole second base and later came around to score. Edwards has now hit safely in eight straight games, recording two extra-base hits, three runs scored, three RBI and two stolen bases during that stretch.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Javier Sanoja has three-hit game Monday
desc: Javier Sanoja went 3-for-5 with a triple, a double, one run scored and three RBI in Monday's 10-7 win over the Colorado Rockies.
impact: Sanoja hit his first triple of the season on Monday, clearing the bases with a three-run triple to right field in the seventh inning. He has now recorded three-hit performances in two of his last three games and is batting .444 with a .667 slugging percentage over his last seven contests.

author: Nicholas Rodriguez
title: Griffin Conine blasts one over fence Monday
desc: Griffin Conine went 1-for-2 with a home run, a walk, two runs scored and three RBI in Monday's 10-7 win over the Colorado Rockies.
impact: Conine pinch-hit for Leo Jimenez in the fifth inning and crushed a towering 433-foot, three-run home run that left the bat at 110.1 mph. He remained in the game, drew a walk in the seventh inning and later came around to score. Since returning from a two-month absence due to injury, Conine is slashing .182/.280/.364 across 22 at-bats.
